## Setup and exact target

Fix the stable pair `(g,n)=(6,6)`. Then

```text
d = 3g − 3 + n = 21.
```

By the revision-2 packet dictionary and `FND-0001`, the unresolved open input for the degree-16 pure-Tate induction at this pair is the pure-weight Borel–Moore group

```text
W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) ≅ W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21),
```

expected of Tate type `Q(8)`. Untwisted, the ordinary pure piece `W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6})` is expected of type `Q(−13)`, corresponding to Chow codimension `d − 8 = 13`.

By `THM-0001`, `H^k(Mbar_{6,6})` is pure of weight `k`. By `THM-0003`, the boundary long exact sequence yields a right-exact sequence

```text
H_{16}(∂Mbar_{6,6}) → H_{16}(Mbar_{6,6}) → W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) → 0.
```

Thus the open pure-weight quotient is precisely the cokernel of boundary homology into compactified homology. The compactified pure-Tate conjecture `CONJ-0001` at this pair is equivalent, after the induction package of `RED-0001`, to showing that this cokernel is a direct sum of `Q(8)`.

## Why this pair is a genuine open base case

By `THM-0004`, in the low-homology induction at degree `k=16`, an open-stratum base case occurs for `n ≥ 2` precisely when

```text
k ≥ 2g − 2 + n.
```

Here `2g − 2 + n = 12 − 2 + 6 = 16`, so equality holds: `(6,6)` is an open base case and cannot be absorbed into vanishing ranges.

By `THM-0005`, the published CKgP bound is `c(6)=5`. Hence `M_{6,6}` lies strictly outside the range where pure-weight cohomology is known to be algebraic/tautological by the CKgP route of `SRC-0002`, Proposition 4.5. The present attempt therefore does **not** extend CKgP; it attacks only the pure-weight Tate type via the weight spectral sequence / decorated graph complex.

## Weight spectral sequence from the normal-crossings compactification

Write `X = Mbar_{6,6}`, `U = M_{6,6}`, and `D = X \ U` for the boundary divisor (normal crossings as a Deligne–Mumford stack). Deligne’s weight spectral sequence for the smooth pair `(X,D)` computes the mixed Hodge structure on the cohomology of `U` (and dually on Borel–Moore / compactly supported cohomology) from the cohomology of the strata

```text
D^{(p)} = disjoint union of codimension-p boundary strata,
```

with differentials given by Gysin/residue maps along inclusions of deeper strata.

Because `U` is smooth of dimension `21`, ordinary cohomology `H^{26}(U)` has weights `≥ 26`, so

```text
W_{26} H^{26}(U) = gr^W_{26} H^{26}(U).
```

Under the Poincaré duality identification of the packet, this graded piece is the ordinary realization of the BM target `W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(U)`. On the spectral-sequence page, only those `E_1` summands whose internal cohomological degree and Tate twist sum to weight `26` in total degree `26` (equivalently, weight `−16` in BM degree `16`) can contribute to this graded piece.

Concretely, boundary strata are indexed by stable dual graphs `Γ` of type `(6,6)`:

```text
M_Γ ≅ (∏_{v ∈ V(Γ)} M_{g(v), n(v)}) / Aut(Γ),
```

with gluing maps from the corresponding compactified products into `D ⊂ X`. Separating nodes give products of two lower moduli stacks; a non-separating node gives a single factor of type `(5,7)` (genus drop by one, marking increase by two legs at the node).

## Decorated graph complex (Getzler–Kapranov form)

The same data assemble into the Getzler–Kapranov decorated graph complex computing the associated graded of the weight filtration on `H^•(M_{g,n})` (equivalently on BM/c-support via duality). A generator in graph degree corresponding to a stable graph `Γ` is an `Aut(Γ)`-invariant pure tensor

```text
⊗_{v ∈ V(Γ)} α_v ,    α_v ∈ H^{•}(M_{g(v), n(v)}),
```

with edge decorations recording the gluing/residue Tate twists `Q(−1)` per node, and with differential the sum of edge contractions and vertex expansions compatible with the modular operad structure.

**Numerical constraints for the pure corner at `(6,6)`.** For a decorated graph to contribute to `gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6})` (equivalently to `W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}`), one must have:

1. `∑_v g(v) + h_1(Γ) = 6` and total legs `n = 6`;
2. stability at every vertex;
3. weight additivity

```text
∑_v wt(α_v) + 2·(# edges contributing Gysin twists) = 26
```

in ordinary cohomological degree `26` after accounting for the dimension shifts on strata;
4. after Poincaré twist by `(21)`, the resulting pure Hodge structure must be compared to `Q(8)`.

Two regimes appear:

- **Top-weight / undecorated regime.** If every vertex is genus `0` and every decoration `α_v` is a unit class, the complex reduces to the commutative graph complex / tropical moduli complex of Chan–Galatius–Payne type. Its cohomology computes top-weight compactly supported graded pieces. Dualizing, this controls a definite corner of the weight filtration, but matching that corner exactly to BM degree `16` / ordinary degree `26` for `(6,6)` is a non-trivial degree check (`GAP-DEGREE-MATCH` below).
- **Decorated regime.** If some vertex has `g(v) > 0` or a positive-degree decoration, the factor `H^{•}(M_{g(v),n(v)})` must itself be pure Tate in the relevant degree for the tensor product to be Tate. Low-degree Tate input is available from `THM-0002` (compactified even degrees `≤ 14`), from `THM-0006`–`THM-0007` in genera `1` and `2`, and from CKgP ranges `THM-0005` when `n(v) ≤ c(g(v))`. Outside those ranges, the decoration may re-introduce an open base case from the finite list in `RED-0001`.

## What can be proved unconditionally from the packet

**Claim A (target identification).** The open input is exactly `W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) ≅ W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21)`, expected `Q(8)`. This is the packet dictionary plus `FND-0001`.

**Claim B (base-case membership).** `(6,6)` satisfies `k = 2g − 2 + n = 16`, hence is an open base case for the degree-16 induction (`THM-0004`).

**Claim C (CKgP unavailable).** `n = 6 > c(6) = 5`, so the published CKgP algebraicity route does not apply (`THM-0005`).

**Claim D (right-exact reduction).** `W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) ≅ coker( H_{16}(∂Mbar_{6,6}) → H_{16}(Mbar_{6,6}) )` as mixed Hodge structures (`THM-0003`).

**Claim E (spectral sequence existence).** The Deligne weight spectral sequence of `(Mbar_{6,6}, ∂)` and the Getzler–Kapranov decorated graph complex both compute the associated graded of the weight filtration on the cohomology of `M_{6,6}`; the pure piece of interest is an `E_∞` subquotient of a finite direct sum of decorated-stratum cohomologies for stable graphs of type `(6,6)`.

**Claim F (boundary strata are products).** Every irreducible boundary stratum is a finite quotient of a product of moduli stacks of strictly simpler stable type (lower total dimension, or lower genus, or a product decomposition). Künneth and purity (`THM-0001`) apply on each compactified factor.

## Reduction of the Tate statement to a finite graph-complex computation

Combining D–F, the pure Tate claim

```text
W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) ≅ ⊕ Q(8)
```

is equivalent to the following finite statement:

> In the weight spectral sequence / decorated graph complex for `(g,n)=(6,6)`, every `E_1` (resp. graph-complex) summand that can contribute to the pure corner of weight `−16` in BM degree `16` is itself pure Tate of type `⊕ Q(8)` after the packet’s Poincaré twist, and all differentials in that corner preserve the Tate subcategory and create no non-split exotic extensions in the `E_∞` subquotient isomorphic to the BM pure piece.

If in addition the undecorated top-weight corner is the only surviving corner (i.e. all positively decorated contributions cancel or land in other weights), the claim further reduces to a single graph-complex cohomology group being a direct sum of trivial Hodge structures of the expected Tate type.

## Explicit gaps (no completeness claimed)

The argument stops short of evaluating that finite complex. The following steps are **not** proved here:

1. **`GAP-DEGREE-MATCH`.** Exact matching of the CGP top-weight degree index to BM degree `16` / ordinary degree `26` for `(6,6)` (including all Tate twists and dimension shifts) is not written out with a complete reference chain inside the supplied packet.
2. **`GAP-GRAPH-ENUMERATION`.** The finite list of stable graphs `Γ` of type `(6,6)` whose numerical weight can hit the pure corner is not enumerated, nor are their automorphism groups and orbit counts.
3. **`GAP-DECORATION-TAUT`.** For decorated vertices with `g(v) > 0`, purity of type of `α_v` is not checked case-by-case; some decorations may require other open pairs from `RED-0001` (e.g. factors related to `(5,8)`, `(7,4)`, `(8,*)`) and are not discharged inside this single-pair packet.
4. **`GAP-DIFFERENTIALS`.** Vanishing or Tate-preserving properties of Gysin/residue differentials (edge contraction in the graph complex) on the pure corner are not computed.
5. **`GAP-EXTENSIONS`.** Even if every graded `E_1` summand is Tate, non-trivial extensions in the mixed Hodge structure could in principle produce non-Tate subquotients only after semisimplification; the packet forbids claiming completeness from a semisimplification. No argument ruling out non-split non-Tate extensions is given.
6. **`GAP-NO-POINTCOUNT`.** No exact point-count, no equivariant stratification rank computation, and no tautological pairing perfectness proof is supplied; none of these is used to claim ranks.

## Conclusion

The weight spectral sequence / decorated graph complex correctly organizes the pure open input for `(6,6)` as an `E_∞` subquotient of a finite decorated-stratum complex, and the packet’s duality dictionary fixes all degrees and twists. Establishing that this subquotient is `⊕ Q(8)` requires a graph-by-graph computation that is not carried out. Accordingly the attempt is **proposed**, not complete, and does not assert `CONJ-0001` for `(6,6)`.
assumptions: The standard Deligne weight spectral sequence for a smooth DM stack with normal-crossings compactification computes the weight filtration on H^*(M_{g,n}) and, dually, on Borel–Moore homology, with E_1 page built from cohomology of boundary strata M_Γ.
The Getzler–Kapranov modular-operad graph complex is a valid computational model for the associated graded of that weight filtration on M_{g,n} with rational coefficients.

Künneth and Poincaré duality for mixed Hodge structures hold for the smooth proper DM stacks Mbar_{g',n'} appearing as vertex factors, with the Tate twist conventions of the packet (Poincaré twist d=21 for (6,6)).

Inductive Tate input for strictly simpler compactified pairs in degrees ≤14 (THM-0002) and for genus 1–2 even cohomology (THM-0006, THM-0007) may be used as decorations when those pairs appear as vertex factors.

claims.statement: For (g,n)=(6,6) one has d=21 and the open induction input is exactly W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) ≅ W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21), expected of Tate type Q(8), with untwisted ordinary type Q(-13) and Chow codimension 13.
The pair (6,6) is an open-stratum base case for the degree-16 low-homology induction because n≥2 and k=16 equals 2g-2+n=16.
Published CKgP does not apply to M_{6,6}, since c(6)=5 < 6; algebraicity of the pure-weight piece cannot be quoted from the CKgP table.
As mixed Hodge structures, W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) is the cokernel of H_{16}(∂Mbar_{6,6}) → H_{16}(Mbar_{6,6}).

The Deligne weight spectral sequence of the normal-crossings compactification Mbar_{6,6} ⊃ ∂, equivalently the Getzler–Kapranov decorated graph complex of stable graphs of type (6,6), computes gr^W of the cohomology of M_{6,6}; the pure piece W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6}) is an E_∞ subquotient of that page.
Every boundary stratum of Mbar_{6,6} is a finite quotient of a product of moduli stacks of strictly simpler stable type, so Künneth and purity apply to compactified stratum cohomology.

W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) is a direct sum of Q(8) if and only if, in the pure weight corner of the weight spectral sequence / decorated graph complex for (6,6), every contributing summand is pure Tate of the expected type and all differentials/extensions on that corner remain within the Tate subcategory.

The undecorated (all vertices genus 0) Getzler–Kapranov / CGP graph complex computes the top-weight compactly supported graded pieces of M_{6,6}, which after Poincaré duality and the packet twist (21) control one definite corner of the weight filtration relevant to the BM pure piece.

The pure corner for BM degree 16 / ordinary degree 26 on (6,6) receives no non-Tate contribution from positively decorated vertices, and all Gysin/residue differentials on that corner vanish or are split Tate morphisms, yielding W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) ≅ ⊕ Q(8).

summary: Sets up the Deligne weight spectral sequence and Getzler–Kapranov decorated graph complex for the pure open input W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) ≅ W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6})(21), reduces contributions to stable dual graphs of type (6,6), and isolates the Tate claim as a finite E_∞ computation that is not carried out.
